title: By late 2026, food-crisis risk is being compounded by conflict, climate variability, high input prices, and shrinking humanitarian finance while the evidence system itself is under strain
source_unit: Global Report on Food Crises 2026 Mid-year Update, summarized by the European Commission Joint Research Centre
geography: Global food-crisis settings assessed through IPC, Cadre Harmonisé, FEWS NET, WFP CARI, HNRP and partner systems; famine-risk focus on Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan

observations.period: August 2026; Global Report on Food Crises 2026 Mid-year Update

acute_food_insecurity.value: Acute food insecurity remains at very high levels across many countries as of August 2026

driver_set.value: Conflict, insecurity, weather extremes, high food and fertilizer prices, El Niño risk, Middle East conflict, and reduced humanitarian funding

late_2026_outlook.value: The update expects new climate, conflict, price, and funding risks to worsen conditions in late 2026 and into 2027

observations.method: Mid-year update to the multi-partner Global Report on Food Crises using acute food-insecurity data from IPC, Cadre Harmonisé, FEWS NET, WFP CARI, humanitarian response plans, and related partner systems.
observations.uncertainty: The update summarizes assessed crisis settings rather than all households globally; conditions, classifications, and forecasts can change quickly with access, harvests, conflict, prices, and humanitarian action.
observations.subgroup: People in acute food crisis, conflict-affected households, displaced populations, food producers, children, markets, humanitarian agencies, and communities exposed to climate variability.
observations.counterinterpretation: Early warning, local production, market support, negotiated access, and humanitarian response can prevent deterioration; a risk outlook is not proof that worsening will occur everywhere.

denominator.unit: Global Report on Food Crises 2026 Mid-year Update financing outlook

humanitarian_oda_decline.unit: percent projected decline in humanitarian official development assistance between 2024 and 2026

food_aid_decline.unit: percent projected decline in food aid between 2024 and 2026

response_capacity.value: Falling aid is identified as a risk multiplier for populations already exposed to conflict, climate shocks, food prices, and displacement

observations.method: European Commission JRC summary of the GRFC 2026 Mid-year Update and its comparison of humanitarian ODA and food-aid trends.
observations.uncertainty: The projected declines depend on definitions, exchange rates, inflation, reporting and donor commitments; aggregate finance does not measure local response quality, targeting, or informal coping.
observations.subgroup: Food-insecure households, displaced populations, humanitarian responders, local organizations, donors, food producers, and governments dependent on external assistance.
observations.counterinterpretation: Funding reductions can sometimes be offset by domestic resources, anticipatory action, local leadership, improved targeting, or development and peace investments, but these are not guaranteed substitutes for emergency food assistance.

observations.period: 2026; famine-risk assessment in the mid-year update

denominator.unit: countries identified with famine risk in the cited mid-year update

famine_risk_countries.unit: countries with famine risk identified in the mid-year update

catastrophe_comparison.value: The update reports an overall decrease in the number of people facing IPC/CH Phase 5 catastrophe conditions compared with 2025 while famine risk remains in three countries

risk_mechanism.value: Highly volatile conflict, insecurity, displacement, weather, markets, and access conditions can sustain famine risk even when aggregate catastrophe counts change

observations.method: JRC summary of GRFC 2026 Mid-year Update famine-risk and acute-food-insecurity classifications.
observations.uncertainty: Famine risk is a warning classification rather than a confirmed famine outcome; assessment quality depends on timely mortality, food-consumption, livelihood, nutrition, and access information.
observations.subgroup: Communities in Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan, displaced people, children, local markets, health and nutrition systems, and humanitarian responders.
observations.counterinterpretation: Famine risk can be reduced by ceasefires, access, food assistance, cash, health and nutrition services, local agricultural support, and diplomatic action; forecast severity does not determine the eventual outcome.

denominator.unit: Global food-crisis monitoring and governance system described by the JRC

network_change.value: The Food Security Information Network was closed in 2025, requiring more intensive support from partners for the 2026 report and mid-year update

data_quality_role.value: The JRC provides technical and advisory support to IPC and Cadre Harmonisé frameworks and contributes to quality assurance

early_warning_infrastructure.value: The JRC ASAP agricultural-production anomaly bulletin feeds IPC/CH analyses and GRFC assessments of climatic vulnerabilities

observations.method: JRC account of the multi-partner GRFC governance, data-quality, and early-warning infrastructure supporting the 2026 mid-year update.
observations.uncertainty: Institutional restructuring can affect continuity, coverage, comparability, and response speed; the public summary does not quantify the effect of FSIN closure on individual country estimates.
observations.subgroup: Food-security analysts, local and international assessment partners, governments, donors, humanitarian agencies, farmers, and crisis-affected populations dependent on early warning and assistance.
observations.counterinterpretation: Consolidating technical support can improve coordination and quality in some settings, while reducing independent capacity, local ownership, or data diversity if funding and institutional safeguards are insufficient.

related_sources.claim: European Commission knowledge portal entry for the 2026 Global Report on Food Crises Mid-year Update.
WFP publication hub for the Global Report on Food Crises series.

boundary: This record is a September 2026 mid-year update to the existing GRFC 2026 signal. It adds late-year conflict, climate, price, funding, famine-risk, and food-security data-system developments; it is not a household food-consumption survey, a complete global census, a causal attribution of each driver, or proof that projected funding declines will produce identical outcomes in every crisis.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official European Commission JRC summary reviewed for August 2026 acute-food-insecurity status, drivers, famine-risk countries, humanitarian ODA and food-aid projections, FSIN closure, JRC quality-assurance role, and ASAP early-warning contribution.
